paper_title: (Almost) Closing the $ν$MSM Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter Window with NuSTAR
coupling_convention: sin²(2θ) where θ is the sterile-active neutrino mixing angle; dimensionless
notes: This paper constrains sterile neutrino dark matter via radiative decay (χ → γν) using NuSTAR observations of the Galactic Center. The primary result is a limit on the mixing angle sin²2θ as a function of sterile neutrino mass m_χ in the range 10–50 keV. However, the paper does not present explicit numerical data points in tabular form. Figure 8 shows the exclusion limit as a red line in the (m_χ, sin²2θ) plane, but precise numerical values cannot be reliably extracted from the figure without access to the underlying data. The coupling type 'sin²2θ' (mixing angle squared) does not map cleanly to the provided enum of coupling types, which are designed for axion-photon, axion-electron, dark photon, and other specific interactions. Sterile neutrino mixing is a distinct parameter space. To properly extract data points, one would need either: (1) a table of (m_χ, sin²2θ) pairs, or (2) access to the figure data files. The paper's main contribution is the exclusion region shown graphically in Figs. 1 and 8, which rules out approximately half of the previously allowed νMSM parameter space in the 10–50 keV mass range. The analysis uses NuSTAR's 0-bounce photons to search for monochromatic X-ray lines at E_γ = m_χ/2 from sterile neutrino decay. No new lines are detected, yielding upper limits on the decay rate Γ (shown in Fig. 7) and corresponding limits on sin²2θ. The confidence level is 95% (one-sided).
